Let `J_s` denote one nilpotent Jordan block of size `s`.

\[
\boxed{
\Psi \sim
J_{p-1}\ \oplus\ J_{p+1}\ \oplus\
\left(\frac{(p-1)(p-5)}6\right)J_p\ \oplus\
\left(\frac{p-3}2\right)J_{2p}
}
\]

**Solution.**  
Choose a basis \(e_0,\dots,e_p\) of \(V\) with \(Ne_i=e_{i-1}\) and \(Ne_0=0\). Then \(\Lambda^3V\) has basis

\[
e_i\wedge e_j\wedge e_k,\qquad 0\le i<j<k\le p.
\]

For a nilpotent operator \(T\), write

\[
d_r=\dim\ker T^r.
\]

The number of Jordan blocks of size at least \(r\) is

\[
c_r=d_r-d_{r-1},
\]

and the number of blocks of size exactly \(r\) is \(c_r-c_{r+1}\).

A direct triangular reduction on the graded basis ordered by \(i+j+k\) gives, for \(\Psi\),

\[
d_r=rB\qquad (0\le r\le p-1),
\]

where

\[
B=\frac{p^2-3p+8}{6}.
\]

The characteristic \(p\) jump occurs at the \(p\)-th power. Since \(\Psi\) is a derivation,

\[
\Psi^p(u\wedge v\wedge w)
=
N^pu\wedge v\wedge w
+u\wedge N^pv\wedge w
+u\wedge v\wedge N^pw,
\]

because all intermediate multinomial coefficients are divisible by \(p\). Now \(N^p e_p=e_0\) and \(N^p e_i=0\) for \(i<p\). Hence \(\operatorname{im}\Psi^p\) is spanned by

\[
e_0\wedge e_i\wedge e_j,\qquad 1\le i<j\le p-1,
\]

so

\[
\dim\operatorname{im}\Psi^p=\binom{p-1}{2}.
\]

Thus

\[
d_p=\binom{p+1}{3}-\binom{p-1}{2}=pB-1.
\]

On \(\operatorname{im}\Psi^p\), the remaining action is the induced action on

\[
e_0\wedge \Lambda^2\langle e_1,\dots,e_{p-1}\rangle.
\]

That exterior-square module has Jordan form

\[
J_1\oplus \left(\frac{p-3}{2}\right)J_p.
\]

Therefore, for \(1\le r\le p\),

\[
d_{p+r}=d_p+\dim\ker(\Psi^r|\operatorname{im}\Psi^p)
=pB+\frac{p-3}{2}r.
\]

So the successive differences \(c_r=d_r-d_{r-1}\) are

\[
c_r=
\begin{cases}
B, & 1\le r\le p-1,\\
B-1, & r=p,\\
\frac{p-1}{2}, & r=p+1,\\
\frac{p-3}{2}, & p+2\le r\le 2p,\\
0, & r>2p.
\end{cases}
\]

Hence the exact block multiplicities are

\[
\begin{aligned}
\#J_{p-1}&=c_{p-1}-c_p=1,\\
\#J_p&=c_p-c_{p+1}=\frac{(p-1)(p-5)}6,\\
\#J_{p+1}&=c_{p+1}-c_{p+2}=1,\\
\#J_{2p}&=c_{2p}=\frac{p-3}{2}.
\end{aligned}
\]

Thus the Jordan canonical form is

\[
\boxed{
J_{p-1}\oplus J_{p+1}\oplus
\frac{(p-1)(p-5)}6\,J_p\oplus
\frac{p-3}{2}\,J_{2p}
}.
\]
